## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Ujjagghika* ("Laughing loudly"), designated as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 11, is a training rule from the Sekhiya section of the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic decorum [SuttaCentral]. Modern English translations of the rule include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. No direct discussions of this rule were identified in the secondary literature sample, where all search hits for "sk 11" correspond either to verse 11 of the classical *Sāṅkhyakārikā* or to unrelated Tibetan pagination.

The rule forms part of a uniform series of etiquette regulations for entering and sitting in inhabited areas. Across the Theravāda tradition, direct parallels occur in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Sekhiya 11), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Sekhiya 11) and Pātimokkha, as well as the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. The rule is extensively attested across early Buddhist monastic lineages: Sanskrit parallels survive in the Prātimokṣa traditions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahāsāṅghika, and Lokottaravāda; and Chinese translations represent the Vinayas of the Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and related recensions [SuttaCentral].

Pali-internal text reuse calculated by DharmaNexus identifies 113 matching passages shared across 45 Pali Vinaya texts, driven by the formulaic legal framing of the Sekhiya rules [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments occur with adjacent Sekhiya rules, particularly Sekhiya 16 (Bu-Vb Sk16, sharing segments §1.1–1.15), Sekhiya 18 (Bu-Vb Sk18, sharing §0.1–1.15), Sekhiya 20 (Bu-Vb Sk20), Sekhiya 10 (Bu-Vb Sk10), and Sekhiya 9 (Bu-Vb Sk9) [DharmaNexus].
